title: Timken India Ltd - 522113 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Timken India Q4 FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for first time, up 14.2% YoY to INR10,731 million; PBT margin 19.3%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue from operations was INR10,731 million (up 14.2% YoY), the first quarter above INR1,000 crore, with PBT of INR2,074 million (19.3% margin) after a labour code impact. FY26 standalone revenue hit a record INR31,478 million (up 8.6%), with PBT of INR5,304 million (up about 3%) and PBT margin of 15.5%. The Board approved merging Timken GGB into Timken India. Management flagged input cost inflation entering FY27, with price pass-through only about 10% achieved so far, and said the new Bharuch plant is ramping slowly with about INR80 crore of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR278 crore (26% of quarterly sales), up from INR128 crore in Q3 but slightly down YoY. FY26 INR781 crore (23%).

segments.name: Mobile others (CV and tractors)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR205 crore (19%), up 22% QoQ. FY26 INR681 crore (20%).

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR162 crore (15%). FY26 INR582 crore (17%).

segments.name: Process industry
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR200 crore (19%). FY26 INR651 crore (19%).

segments.name: Exports (intercompany)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 INR222 crore (21%), up about 40% QoQ from INR159 crore in Q3 and up about 66% YoY on the full year. FY26 INR707 crore (21%).

segments.name: GGB (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR16.6 crore and PBT INR4.6 crore, a PBT margin of about 30-32%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 top-line growth above market growth and says it will outgrow the market; no numerical revenue or margin guidance was given.

Price increases to offset raw material inflation (steel, grinding wheels, coolants, currency): about 10% achieved as of the call, with the aim of completing most of the pass-through over the current and next quarter.
Bharuch CRB/SRB plant expected to reach about 70% utilisation by July-August 2026, improving monthly after that.
Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR120 crore capex): first production targeted for November-December 2026, with asset turns of about 2x to start.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of revenue (management pegged last two years at about 8.5%), covering Jamshedpur rail, GGB plain bearings at Bharuch and some heat-treatment investment.
Management said the 65:35 domestic-manufactured to imported mix may hold for the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bharuch new plant: all lines capitalised; smaller lines and spherical lines running near full, large-line PPAPs under way, and CRB lines running close to two shifts. More than 100 new part introductions underway. FY26 revenue from the plant about INR80 crore (Q4 about INR60 crore, Q3 about INR12 crore). Management said the plant is still close to breakeven.

Bharuch total investment about INR720 crore including forex; buildings about INR350 crore; plant and machinery roughly INR310-320 crore by management's estimate. Peak revenue said to be close to 2x asset turns, but management ruled out INR1,000 crore.
Jamshedpur rail expansion: about INR120 crore capex, imported robotic machines from Europe, all approvals in place. Management said the building was built with spare capacity.
Plain bearing expansion at Bharuch and renewable energy investments are progressing; management said both are broadly on track.
Capital is debt-free; management said it will consider further expansion (0-8 inch range for CV and tractors, M&A) if the project is right.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is stable across most segments and is not among its top three concerns; cost escalation and pass-through, Bharuch ramp-up/PPAP, and expansion projects are the top three.
Steel MRO is slow and steel melt was lower in the quarter; cement MRO is good. OE sentiment is wait-and-watch because of geopolitics.
North America export demand is gaining momentum even without a signed US trade deal; the US is about 50% of exports, per the analyst.
CV demand described as robust with cyclicality; tractors okay; rail slow and steady; aftermarket okay.
Pricing: price increases began mid-April 2026 for both pass-through and recovery; about 10% realised, with automotive customers expected to delay. Management hopes for retrospective recovery.
Management said the Indian bearing market is about USD 2-2.5 billion (about 65% mobile, 35% stationary) and expects process and distribution to grow fastest.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken to offset raw material inflation, and will there be margin pressure in the next 1-2 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Price pass-through has only begun, at about 10%; management expects the rest over the current and next quarter, with the automotive OEM segment lagging. Management did not quantify the margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for domestic rail, CV, and US exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 exports were INR222 crore (up about 40% QoQ, up about 66% YoY for the full year); rail was INR278 crore in Q4 (slight YoY decline); CV described as robust.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch utilisation targets and FY26 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue about INR80 crore; utilisation expected to reach about 70% by July-August 2026, then improve monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Segment split for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4: rail 26%, mobile others 19%, distribution 15%, process 19%, exports 21% (total INR1,073 crore including intercompany). FY26 total INR3,419 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Jamshedpur capex timeline and asset turns; FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Production targeted for November-December 2026 at about 2x asset turns to start. FY27 capex expected at 8-10% of revenue; no formal capex guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend level?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY26 final dividend was INR2.5 per share on INR10 face value, down from INR36 previously. Management said it pays large dividends every 3-4 years and will consider the shareholder's request.

risks_watch: Raw material and currency inflation may outpace price recovery; only about 10% of pass-through was achieved at the call.
Bharuch ramp-up depends on PPAP and customer approvals, and the plant is still near breakeven; the 70% utilisation target is by July-August 2026.
Steel MRO softness and wait-and-watch OE sentiment amid geopolitical uncertainty.
Dependence on North American exports and the unsigned US trade deal.
Imported share of sales is about 35%, and the trading mix will remain exposed to currency moves.
Jamshedpur rail commissioning (about INR120 crore) is targeted for December 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, but cautious on cost pressure and the Bharuch ramp-up timing. Management declined to give numerical FY27 revenue or margin guidance, and it acknowledged a slight delay at Bharuch.
key_quotes: So, margins and revenue both, we want to be more than the market growth.
And we hope between this quarter and next quarter, we should be able to pass it on.
So demand is not currently an issue.
I would say that 65%-35% might be there for next 2, 3 years, easy, but the pie will keep on increasing.
